title: The Owner of Calvin Klein Cuts Office Jobs

source.author: Dani James
source.title: Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger owner to cut 4% of workforce

paragraphs: PVH is an American fashion company. It owns two famous brands, Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger. On November 12, 2026, Retail Dive reported that PVH plans to cut about 4% of its workers around the world. The news came from a report that PVH sent to a government office in the United States.

The cuts are not the same for every kind of job. They focus on people who do not work with shoppers. In other words, most of them work in offices, not in stores. The cuts are equal to about 12% of the company's office workers. For those people and their colleagues, this is hard news.

Why is PVH doing this? The company says it wants to be more productive. Productivity means how much work a company gets done with the people and money it has. PVH wants to eliminate work that is done twice. It also wants fewer levels of managers. It calls this a simpler way of working.

The plan will proceed fast. The cuts began at once, and PVH expects to finish them within the first quarter of 2027. The company also expects to save 100 million dollars in its 2027 business year. Not all of this will come from jobs. PVH says the savings will come from people and from other costs too.

PVH does not only want to cut. It also wants to invest in new products, in the way it moves its goods, and in online sales. So the company is trying to tackle two things at once: lower costs and future growth.

The underlying problem is weak sales. In the second quarter, PVH's revenue fell 3% from a year earlier, to about 2 billion dollars. Tommy Hilfiger's revenue was about flat. Calvin Klein's revenue dropped 7%. Sales fell in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and the Americas. They grew a little in the Asia Pacific region.

For the full year, PVH still expects revenue to be flat compared with the year before. That is not a bright prospect, but it may be a realistic one. Experts at the company Jefferies wrote about PVH in October. They called online sales the strongest sign that the money put into the brands is working. Nevertheless, they said that Europe is under heavy pressure and that next year is not certain.

This story highlights a hard choice. A company can eliminate jobs quickly, and this can make it more productive for a while. But cutting alone cannot overcome the underlying problem. To overcome weak sales, PVH needs products that shoppers want. The colleagues who stay will have to tackle that job. The two brands are distinct, and Calvin Klein's sales fell more. Higher productivity helps only if sales proceed in the right direction too.
